frozen_prediction: After rehydration, low-risk/basic functions can restart before genome restoration is complete, while proliferation/developmental progression should restart on a later permission clock associated with recovery from damage.
preregistered_threshold: >=3 independently evolved lineages with matched evidence that high-risk restart is temporally separated from basic-function recovery; causal promotion requires direct perturbation showing that damage-repair/checkpoint status shifts restart timing.

whole_larva.basic_function: physiological activity returns within ~1 h after rehydration
whole_larva.genome_integrity: nuclear DNA restoration after anhydrobiosis typically requires ~72-96 h in comet/TEM assays
whole_larva.interpretation: basic organismal function resumes long before whole-nuclear-DNA integrity is restored

pv11_cell_line.origin: embryonic cell line derived from P. vanderplanki
rehydration_early_function: mitochondrial membrane potential can recover within ~30 min in preconditioned Pv11 cells
a preserved membrane-protein response is detectable ~1 h after rehydration in a 2025 engineered Pv11 line
de-novo-protein-dependent sensory response emerges from ~12 h and is strongly recovered by ~24 h
dna_repair_program: Pv11 transcriptomes sampled at 3 h and 24 h after rehydration show recovery-associated DNA-repair activity
a RAD16-like gene is specifically elevated at R3
NER-associated genes are elevated during rehydration including at R24
later transcriptomic work sampled R3/R12/R24/R72 and explicitly links rehydration-associated DNA-repair programs to recovery and resumption of proliferation

proliferation_clock.1_to_48_h: live-cell concentration remains essentially stable; no significant growth
proliferation_clock.144_h: growth reaches a plateau in the 2025 time series

pv11_cell_line.strongest_bridge: EARLY FUNCTION 1-24 h -> DNA-REPAIR PROGRAM 3-24 h -> CELL NUMBER FLAT THROUGH 48 h -> SIGNIFICANT PROLIFERATION FROM 72 h

supporting_damage_load_test.source_class: JAEA technical annual-report evidence; supportive, below peer-reviewed causal tier
supporting_damage_load_test.observation: dried Pv11 cells exposed to larger ionizing-radiation damage showed delayed return to normal proliferation; 480 Gy samples were reported to begin normal proliferation around ~2 weeks rather than within ~1 week for lower-dose/control samples
supporting_damage_load_test.interpretation: damage load covaries with proliferation restart delay, but this is not accepted here as definitive repair-checkpoint causality

promote.reason: Bacillus, Adineta and Polypedilum/Pv11 now provide three independently evolved lineages showing multi-clock recovery with later high-risk restart or high-fidelity genome handling.

hold.reason: Polypedilum still lacks a direct matched perturbation in which DNA-repair/checkpoint impairment is shown to delay or deregulate the 72 h proliferation restart.

revised_operator.name: RISK_STRATIFIED_REENTRY_PERMISSION_GRAPH
revised_operator.formula: REHYDRATION -> EARLY FUNCTION -> DAMAGE_PROCESSING -> FUNCTION_SPECIFIC_PERMISSION -> HIGH_RISK_RESTART -> STABLE_HOMEOSTASIS
revised_operator.important: This is a cross-kingdom functional abstraction, not evidence for a conserved molecular pathway.

next_decisive_experiment.test: Measure DNA damage or repair-state and cell-cycle entry in the same rehydration experiment at dense time points from 0-96 h, then perturb a repair/checkpoint component and test whether the onset of S phase/proliferation shifts.
next_decisive_experiment.kill_rule: If proliferation onset is unchanged despite experimentally increasing unresolved DNA damage or impairing relevant repair/checkpoint activity, the causal high-risk permission-gate model is weakened or rejected for Polypedilum.

claim_ceiling: SAME SPECIES DIFFERENT EXPERIMENTS != MATCHED SINGLE-EXPERIMENT CAUSALITY
NO HUMAN LONGEVITY OR THERAPEUTIC CLAIM
